10	
11	Continuation of `AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.P1`: the overlap `D₊(X₀X₁)` of the two standard
12	charts of `P1 k` and its identification with the Laurent polynomial ring, the section-level
13	chart identifications, and the bundled chart package.

15	* `P1.overlapAlgEquiv : (k[X₀,X₁]_(X₀X₁))₀ ≃ₐ[k] k[T,T⁻¹]`, with the two restriction maps
16	  `P1.awayToOverlapLeft/Right` becoming `t ↦ T` and `t ↦ T⁻¹`
17	  (`P1.overlapAlgEquiv_awayToOverlapLeft`/`Right`);
18	* the *Laurent span* property `P1.exists_awayToOverlap_add`: every element of the overlap
19	  ring is a sum of restrictions from the two charts;
20	* section-level versions of all of the above (`P1.chartSectionsEquiv₀/₁`,
21	  `P1.overlapSectionsEquiv`, `P1.overlapSectionsEquiv_res_left/right`);
22	* the package `AlgebraicGeometry.LaurentChartPair` with canonical term
23	  `P1.laurentChartPair k`, and the span property `LaurentChartPair.exists_res_add_res`
24	  for any such package. This package is exactly what the two-lattice finiteness argument
25	  for `H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` consumes.
26	-/

42	/-- The standard grading of `k[X₀, X₁]`, the graded ring underlying `P1 k`. -/
43	local notation "𝒜" => homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k

45	/-! ### The overlap `D₊(X₀X₁)` and the identification with Laurent polynomials -/
46	
47	/-- The restriction map from the chart `D₊(X₀)` to the overlap `D₊(X₀X₁)`. -/
48	noncomputable def awayToOverlapLeft :
49	    Away 𝒜 (X 0) →+* Away 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1) :=
50	  awayMap 𝒜 (X_mem k 1) rfl
51	
52	/-- The restriction map from the chart `D₊(X₁)` to the overlap `D₊(X₀X₁)`. -/
53	noncomputable def awayToOverlapRight :
54	    Away 𝒜 (X 1) →+* Away 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1) :=
55	  awayMap 𝒜 (X_mem k 0) (mul_comm (X 0) (X 1))
56	
57	theorem awayToOverlapLeft_eq :
58	    awayToOverlapLeft k = awayMap 𝒜 (X_mem k 1)
59	      (rfl : (X 0 : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) * X 1 = X 0 * X 1) :=
60	  rfl
61	
62	theorem awayToOverlapRight_eq :
63	    awayToOverlapRight k = awayMap 𝒜 (X_mem k 0) (mul_comm (X 0) (X 1)) :=
64	  rfl
65	
66	theorem awayToOverlapLeft_algebraMap (r : k) :
67	    awayToOverlapLeft k (algebraMap k _ r) = algebraMap k _ r :=
68	  awayMap_fromZeroRingHom 𝒜 (X_mem k 1)
69	    (rfl : (X 0 : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) * X 1 = X 0 * X 1) (algebraMap k (𝒜 0) r)
70	
71	theorem awayToOverlapRight_algebraMap (r : k) :
72	    awayToOverlapRight k (algebraMap k _ r) = algebraMap k _ r :=
73	  awayMap_fromZeroRingHom 𝒜 (X_mem k 0) (mul_comm (X 0) (X 1))
74	    (algebraMap k (𝒜 0) r)
75	
76	noncomputable instance : Algebra (Away 𝒜 (X 0)) (Away 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1)) :=
77	  (awayToOverlapLeft k).toAlgebra
78	
79	noncomputable instance : Algebra (Away 𝒜 (X 1)) (Away 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1)) :=
80	  (awayToOverlapRight k).toAlgebra

82	theorem isLocalizationElem_eq :
83	    Away.isLocalizationElem (X_mem k 0) (X_mem k 1) = chartCoord k 0 1 := by
84	  rw [Away.isLocalizationElem, chartCoord_eq]
85	  congr 1
86	  exact pow_one _

90	instance : IsLocalization.Away (chartCoord k 0 1) (Away 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1)) := by
91	  have h : IsLocalization.Away (Away.isLocalizationElem (X_mem k 0) (X_mem k 1))
92	      (Away 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1)) :=

99	noncomputable def overlapRingEquiv :
100	    Away 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1) ≃+* LaurentPolynomial k :=
101	  IsLocalization.ringEquivOfRingEquiv (M := Submonoid.powers (chartCoord k 0 1))
102	    (T := Submonoid.powers (Polynomial.X : Polynomial k))
103	    (Away 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1)) (LaurentPolynomial k)
104	    (awayAlgEquiv k fin_zero_ne_one).toRingEquiv

106	        exact congrArg _ (awayAlgEquiv_chartCoord k fin_zero_ne_one))

108	theorem overlapRingEquiv_awayToOverlapLeft (z : Away 𝒜 (X 0)) :
109	    overlapRingEquiv k (awayToOverlapLeft k z) =
110	      Polynomial.toLaurent (awayAlgEquiv k fin_zero_ne_one z) := by
111	  rw [← LaurentPolynomial.algebraMap_eq_toLaurent]
112	  exact IsLocalization.ringEquivOfRingEquiv_eq _ _

116	noncomputable def overlapAlgEquiv :
117	    Away 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1) ≃ₐ[k] LaurentPolynomial k :=
118	  { overlapRingEquiv k with
119	    commutes' := fun r => by
120	      change overlapRingEquiv k (algebraMap k _ r) = _
121	      rw [← awayToOverlapLeft_algebraMap, overlapRingEquiv_awayToOverlapLeft,
122	        AlgEquiv.commutes, ← Polynomial.C_eq_algebraMap, Polynomial.toLaurent_C,
123	        LaurentPolynomial.C_eq_algebraMap] }

125	theorem overlapAlgEquiv_apply (z : Away 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1)) :
126	    overlapAlgEquiv k z = overlapRingEquiv k z :=
127	  rfl

130	canonical map `k[t] → k[T,T⁻¹]`, `t ↦ T`. -/
131	theorem overlapAlgEquiv_awayToOverlapLeft (z : Away 𝒜 (X 0)) :
132	    overlapAlgEquiv k (awayToOverlapLeft k z) =
133	      Polynomial.toLaurent (awayAlgEquiv k fin_zero_ne_one z) :=
134	  overlapRingEquiv_awayToOverlapLeft k z

136	theorem awayToOverlap_mul_eq_one :
137	    awayToOverlapLeft k (chartCoord k 0 1) * awayToOverlapRight k (chartCoord k 1 0) = 1 := by
138	  rw [awayToOverlapLeft_eq, awayToOverlapRight_eq, chartCoord_eq k 0 1, chartCoord_eq k 1 0,

141	    Localization.r_iff_exists]

144	theorem overlapAlgEquiv_awayToOverlapRight_chartCoord :
145	    overlapAlgEquiv k (awayToOverlapRight k (chartCoord k 1 0)) = LaurentPolynomial.T (-1) := by
146	  have h1 : (LaurentPolynomial.T 1 : LaurentPolynomial k) *
147	      overlapAlgEquiv k (awayToOverlapRight k (chartCoord k 1 0)) = 1 := by
148	    rw [show (LaurentPolynomial.T 1 : LaurentPolynomial k) = Polynomial.toLaurent Polynomial.X
149	        from Polynomial.toLaurent_X.symm,
150	      ← awayAlgEquiv_chartCoord k fin_zero_ne_one,
151	      ← overlapAlgEquiv_awayToOverlapLeft, ← map_mul, awayToOverlap_mul_eq_one, map_one]
152	  calc overlapAlgEquiv k (awayToOverlapRight k (chartCoord k 1 0))
153	      = (LaurentPolynomial.T (-1) * LaurentPolynomial.T 1) *
154	          overlapAlgEquiv k (awayToOverlapRight k (chartCoord k 1 0)) := by
155	        rw [← LaurentPolynomial.T_add, neg_add_cancel, LaurentPolynomial.T_zero, one_mul]
156	    _ = LaurentPolynomial.T (-1) := by rw [mul_assoc, h1, mul_one]

158	/-- Through the chart identifications, the right restriction map to the overlap is the map
159	`k[t] → k[T,T⁻¹]`, `t ↦ T⁻¹`. -/
160	theorem overlapAlgEquiv_awayToOverlapRight (z : Away 𝒜 (X 1)) :
161	    overlapAlgEquiv k (awayToOverlapRight k z) =
162	      Polynomial.aeval (LaurentPolynomial.T (-1) : LaurentPolynomial k)
163	        (awayAlgEquiv k fin_one_ne_zero z) := by
164	  obtain ⟨p, rfl⟩ := polyToAway_surjective k fin_one_ne_zero z
165	  rw [awayAlgEquiv_polyToAway]
166	  induction p using Polynomial.induction_on' with
167	  | add f g hf hg => simp only [map_add, hf, hg]
168	  | monomial n a =>
169	    simp only [polyToAway_monomial, map_mul, map_pow,
170	      overlapAlgEquiv_awayToOverlapRight_chartCoord, awayToOverlapRight_algebraMap,
171	      AlgEquiv.commutes, Polynomial.aeval_monomial]

173	/-! ### The Laurent span property on the overlap -/
174	
175	/-- **Laurent span, ring level**: every element of the overlap ring is the sum of a
176	restriction from the left chart and a restriction from the right chart. -/
177	theorem exists_awayToOverlap_add (w : Away 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1)) :
178	    ∃ (p : Away 𝒜 (X 0)) (q : Away 𝒜 (X 1)),
179	      w = awayToOverlapLeft k p + awayToOverlapRight k q := by
180	  obtain ⟨f₁, f₂, hf⟩ := LaurentPolynomial.exists_toLaurent_add_aeval (overlapAlgEquiv k w)
181	  refine ⟨(awayAlgEquiv k fin_zero_ne_one).symm f₁,
182	    (awayAlgEquiv k fin_one_ne_zero).symm f₂, (overlapAlgEquiv k).injective ?_⟩
183	  rw [map_add, overlapAlgEquiv_awayToOverlapLeft, overlapAlgEquiv_awayToOverlapRight,
184	    AlgEquiv.apply_symm_apply, AlgEquiv.apply_symm_apply, hf]

186	/-! ### Section-level identifications -/
187	
188	theorem awayToSection_surjective {m : ℕ} (f : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) (f_deg : f ∈ 𝒜 m)
189	    (hm : 0 < m) : Function.Surjective (Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 f).hom := fun z => by
190	  obtain ⟨w, hw⟩ := (Proj.basicOpenIsoAway 𝒜 f f_deg hm).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv.surjective z
191	  exact ⟨w, hw⟩

193	theorem overlap_le_left : Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1) ≤ chartOpen k 0 :=
194	  Proj.basicOpen_mono 𝒜 _ _ ⟨X 1, rfl⟩
195	
196	theorem overlap_le_right : Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1) ≤ chartOpen k 1 :=

205	    ((P1 k).presheaf.map (homOfLE (overlap_le_left k)).op).hom

298	        (chartSectionsEquiv₁ k b) := by

306	
307	/-- A **Laurent chart pair** on the projective line over `k`: two affine opens covering
308	`P1 k` with a distinguished affine overlap, whose section rings are polynomial rings `k[t]`,
309	whose overlap section ring is the Laurent polynomial ring, and such that the two restriction
310	maps become `t ↦ T` and `t ↦ T⁻¹`.
311	
312	The canonical example is `P1.laurentChartPair k` (the two standard charts). The Laurent span
313	property `LaurentChartPair.exists_res_add_res` holds for any such pair; this package is
314	exactly what the two-lattice finiteness argument for `H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` consumes. -/
315	structure LaurentChartPair (k : Type u) [Field k] where
316	  /-- The left chart. -/
317	  U₀ : (P1 k).Opens
318	  /-- The right chart. -/
319	  U₁ : (P1 k).Opens
320	  /-- The overlap. -/
321	  U₀₁ : (P1 k).Opens
322	  le_left : U₀₁ ≤ U₀
323	  le_right : U₀₁ ≤ U₁
324	  inf_eq : U₀ ⊓ U₁ = U₀₁
325	  isAffineOpen_U₀ : IsAffineOpen U₀
326	  isAffineOpen_U₁ : IsAffineOpen U₁
327	  isAffineOpen_U₀₁ : IsAffineOpen U₀₁
328	  /-- The two charts cover `P1 k`. -/
329	  sup_eq_top : U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤
330	  /-- The sections on the left chart form a polynomial ring. -/
331	  Γ₀ : Γ(P1 k, U₀) ≃+* Polynomial k
332	  /-- The sections on the right chart form a polynomial ring. -/
333	  Γ₁ : Γ(P1 k, U₁) ≃+* Polynomial k
334	  /-- The sections on the overlap form a Laurent polynomial ring. -/
335	  Γ₀₁ : Γ(P1 k, U₀₁) ≃+* LaurentPolynomial k
336	  /-- Through the identifications, restriction from the left chart is `t ↦ T`. -/
337	  res_left : ∀ a, Γ₀₁ (((P1 k).presheaf.map (homOfLE le_left).op).hom a) =
338	    Polynomial.toLaurent (Γ₀ a)
339	  /-- Through the identifications, restriction from the right chart is `t ↦ T⁻¹`. -/
340	  res_right : ∀ b, Γ₀₁ (((P1 k).presheaf.map (homOfLE le_right).op).hom b) =
341	    Polynomial.aeval (LaurentPolynomial.T (-1) : LaurentPolynomial k) (Γ₁ b)
342	
343	namespace LaurentChartPair

345	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (D : LaurentChartPair k)
346	
347	/-- **Laurent span** for any Laurent chart pair: every section on the overlap is the sum of a
348	restriction from the left chart and a restriction from the right chart. This is the
349	surjectivity half of the Mayer–Vietoris difference map for the two-chart cover. -/
350	theorem exists_res_add_res (z : Γ(P1 k, D.U₀₁)) :
351	    ∃ (a : Γ(P1 k, D.U₀)) (b : Γ(P1 k, D.U₁)),
352	      z = ((P1 k).presheaf.map (homOfLE D.le_left).op).hom a +
353	          ((P1 k).presheaf.map (homOfLE D.le_right).op).hom b := by
354	  obtain ⟨p, q, hpq⟩ := LaurentPolynomial.exists_toLaurent_add_aeval (D.Γ₀₁ z)
355	  refine ⟨D.Γ₀.symm p, D.Γ₁.symm q, D.Γ₀₁.injective ?_⟩
356	  rw [map_add, D.res_left, D.res_right, RingEquiv.apply_symm_apply,
357	    RingEquiv.apply_symm_apply, hpq]
358	
359	end LaurentChartPair

11	/-!
12	# The units of a Laurent polynomial ring over a domain (mathlib supplement)
13	
14	`R[T;T⁻¹]ˣ = Rˣ × ℤ` when `R` is a domain: every unit is `C c * T n` with `c` a unit of `R`,
15	and the exponent `n` is determined.  **Mathlib does not have this.**  The whole `IsUnit` API
16	of `Mathlib/Algebra/Polynomial/Laurent.lean` is the single lemma
17	`LaurentPolynomial.isUnit_T` (measured: `loogle` for `LaurentPolynomial, IsUnit` returns only
18	that, `(LaurentPolynomial ?R)ˣ` returns nothing, and `grep` of the mathlib file confirms one
19	`IsUnit` declaration).  The polynomial analogue `Polynomial.isUnit_iff` *is* in mathlib; the
20	Laurent case is missing because `T (-1)` is a unit, so there is no degree-zero argument.
21	
22	## Why this is here
23	
24	It is the multiplicative half of the `ℙ¹` chart data.  `Curve/P1Charts.lean` identifies the
25	overlap ring of the two standard charts with `LaurentPolynomial k` and provides the *additive*
26	Laurent span (`exists_res_add_res`), which is what computes `H¹(ℙ¹, 𝒪)`.  Computing
27	`Pic(ℙ¹)` instead needs the *unit group* of that same overlap ring modulo the images of the two
28	chart unit groups, and `Rˣ × ℤ` modulo `Rˣ` on each side is where the `ℤ` comes from.
29	
30	## The proof, and the one place a hypothesis is used
31	
32	Clear denominators (`LaurentPolynomial.exists_T_pow`): `f * T^a` and `f⁻¹ * T^b` are honest
33	polynomials whose product is `X ^ (a+b)`.  So the numerator divides a power of `X`, and
34	`X` is prime in `R[X]` **because `R` is a domain** — this is the only use of `IsDomain`.
35	
36	**It is not removable, and that is a THEOREM here rather than a remark.**  An earlier version
37	of this header asserted the counterexample in prose, unverified (`I-1634`).  It is now
38	`isUnit_one_add_C_mul_T_of_sq_eq_zero` together with
39	`not_exists_eq_C_mul_T_one_add_C_mul_T`: whenever `e² = 0`, the element `1 + C e * T 1` is a
40	unit of `R[T;T⁻¹]` over **any** commutative ring, and whenever `e ≠ 0` it is not `C c * T n` for
41	any `c, n`.  Both hold with no domain hypothesis, and `k[ε]/ε²` supplies such an `e`, so the
42	classification genuinely fails there.  It cost fifteen lines; prose cost a reviewer more than
43	that to check.
44	
45	## Main declarations
46	
47	* `LaurentPolynomial.isUnit_iff_C_mul_T` — **the classification**, as an iff.
48	* `LaurentPolynomial.exists_eq_C_mul_T_of_isUnit` — its forward half, in the form consumers use.
49	* `LaurentPolynomial.isUnit_C_mul_T` — the converse half, over any commutative ring.
50	* `LaurentPolynomial.exp_unique` / `coeff_unique` — the exponent and coefficient are determined
51	  by the element (no domain hypothesis; the `omit` markers are the measurement).
52	* `LaurentPolynomial.unitsEquiv` — the unit group as `Rˣ × ℤ`, which is the form the Picard
53	  computation consumes.
54	* `LaurentPolynomial.isUnit_one_add_C_mul_T_of_sq_eq_zero` /
55	  `not_exists_eq_C_mul_T_one_add_C_mul_T` — **the domain hypothesis is necessary**, formalized
56	  rather than asserted.
57	-/
58	
59	set_option autoImplicit false
60	
61	universe u
62	
63	open Polynomial
64	
65	namespace LaurentPolynomial
66	
67	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
68	
69	/-! ## The easy direction, over an arbitrary commutative ring -/
70	
71	/-- A Laurent monomial with unit coefficient is a unit.  No domain hypothesis. -/
72	theorem isUnit_C_mul_T {c : R} (hc : IsUnit c) (n : ℤ) :
73	    IsUnit (LaurentPolynomial.C c * T n) :=
74	  (hc.map LaurentPolynomial.C).mul (isUnit_T n)
75	
76	/-! ## The exponent is determined
77	
78	Stated separately from the classification because it needs no domain hypothesis, and because
79	it is what makes `Pic(ℙ¹) ≅ ℤ` rather than merely a quotient of `ℤ`: without it the exponent
80	would be only a choice. -/
81	
82	/-- **The exponent of a Laurent monomial is determined by the element**, as soon as its
83	coefficient is nonzero.  Evaluated at the index `n`, the two `Finsupp.single`s give `c` and
84	`0`. -/
85	theorem exp_unique {c d : R} (hc : c ≠ 0) {n m : ℤ}
86	    (h : (LaurentPolynomial.C c * T n : LaurentPolynomial R) = LaurentPolynomial.C d * T m) :
87	    n = m := by
88	  by_contra hne
89	  have h1 := congrArg (fun f : LaurentPolynomial R => f n) h
90	  simp only [← LaurentPolynomial.single_eq_C_mul_T] at h1
91	  rw [show (AddMonoidAlgebra.single n c : LaurentPolynomial R) = Finsupp.single n c from rfl,
92	      show (AddMonoidAlgebra.single m d : LaurentPolynomial R) = Finsupp.single m d from rfl,
93	      Finsupp.single_eq_same] at h1
94	  rw [Finsupp.single_apply, if_neg (fun hh : m = n => absurd hh.symm hne)] at h1
95	  exact hc h1
96	
97	/-! ## The domain hypothesis is necessary
98	
99	Not a remark: the two halves below are the counterexample, formalized.  Over a ring with a
100	nonzero square-zero element the classification fails, so `IsDomain` in the next section cannot
101	be dropped.  Neither statement needs a domain, which is the point. -/
102	
103	/-- Over **any** commutative ring, `1 + C e * T 1` is a unit as soon as `e² = 0`: its inverse is
104	`1 - C e * T 1`, because the cross term carries `e²`. -/
105	theorem isUnit_one_add_C_mul_T_of_sq_eq_zero {e : R} (he : e * e = 0) :
106	    IsUnit (1 + LaurentPolynomial.C e * T 1 : LaurentPolynomial R) := by
107	  have hsq : (LaurentPolynomial.C e * T 1) * (LaurentPolynomial.C e * T (1 : ℤ))
108	      = LaurentPolynomial.C (e * e) * T (2 : ℤ) := by
109	    rw [map_mul, show (LaurentPolynomial.C e * T 1) * (LaurentPolynomial.C e * T (1 : ℤ))
110	      = (LaurentPolynomial.C e * LaurentPolynomial.C e) * (T 1 * T (1 : ℤ)) from by ring,
111	      ← T_add]
112	    norm_num
113	  refine ⟨⟨1 + LaurentPolynomial.C e * T 1, 1 - LaurentPolynomial.C e * T 1, ?_, ?_⟩, rfl⟩
114	  · rw [show (1 + LaurentPolynomial.C e * T 1) * (1 - LaurentPolynomial.C e * T (1 : ℤ))
115	      = 1 - (LaurentPolynomial.C e * T 1) * (LaurentPolynomial.C e * T (1 : ℤ)) from by ring,
116	      hsq, he, map_zero, zero_mul, sub_zero]
117	  · rw [show (1 - LaurentPolynomial.C e * T 1) * (1 + LaurentPolynomial.C e * T (1 : ℤ))
118	      = 1 - (LaurentPolynomial.C e * T 1) * (LaurentPolynomial.C e * T (1 : ℤ)) from by ring,
119	      hsq, he, map_zero, zero_mul, sub_zero]
120	
121	/-- The coefficient of a Laurent monomial at an arbitrary index. -/
122	theorem C_mul_T_apply (c : R) (n m : ℤ) :
123	    (LaurentPolynomial.C c * T n : LaurentPolynomial R) m = if n = m then c else 0 := by
124	  rw [← LaurentPolynomial.single_eq_C_mul_T,
125	    show (AddMonoidAlgebra.single n c : LaurentPolynomial R) = Finsupp.single n c from rfl,
126	    Finsupp.single_apply]
127	
128	/-- **The other half of the counterexample**: with `e ≠ 0`, the unit `1 + C e * T 1` is not a
129	monomial `C c * T n`.  It has nonzero coefficients at both `0` and `1`, and a monomial has at
130	most one. -/
131	theorem not_exists_eq_C_mul_T_one_add_C_mul_T [Nontrivial R] {e : R} (he : e ≠ 0) :
132	    ¬ ∃ (c : R) (n : ℤ),
133	      (1 + LaurentPolynomial.C e * T 1 : LaurentPolynomial R) = LaurentPolynomial.C c * T n := by
134	  rintro ⟨c, n, h⟩
135	  have key : ∀ m : ℤ, (1 : LaurentPolynomial R) m + (if (1 : ℤ) = m then e else 0)
136	      = (if n = m then c else 0) := fun m => by
137	    simpa [C_mul_T_apply] using congrArg (fun f : LaurentPolynomial R => f m) h
138	  have hone : ∀ m : ℤ, (1 : LaurentPolynomial R) m = if (0 : ℤ) = m then (1 : R) else 0 :=
139	    fun m => by
140	      rw [show (1 : LaurentPolynomial R) = LaurentPolynomial.C (1 : R) * T (0 : ℤ) from by simp]
141	      exact C_mul_T_apply 1 0 m
142	  have h0 := key 0
143	  have h1 := key 1
144	  rw [hone] at h0 h1
145	  norm_num at h0 h1
146	  by_cases hn : n = 0
147	  · rw [if_pos hn] at h0
148	    rw [if_neg (by omega : ¬ n = 1)] at h1
149	    exact he h1
150	  · exact one_ne_zero ((if_neg hn) ▸ h0)
151	
152	/-! ## The classification -/
153	
154	variable [IsDomain R]
155	
156	/-- **Every unit of `R[T;T⁻¹]` over a domain is `C c * T n` with `c` a unit.**
157	
158	Clear denominators to get polynomials `p, q` with `p * q = X ^ (a + b)`; then `p ∣ X ^ (a+b)`
159	and `X` is prime, so `p` is a unit times `X ^ i`, and the polynomial unit is a constant by
160	`Polynomial.isUnit_iff`. -/
161	theorem exists_eq_C_mul_T_of_isUnit {f : LaurentPolynomial R} (hf : IsUnit f) :
162	    ∃ (c : R) (n : ℤ), IsUnit c ∧ f = LaurentPolynomial.C c * T n := by
163	  obtain ⟨g, hg⟩ := hf.exists_right_inv
164	  obtain ⟨a, p, hp⟩ := exists_T_pow f
165	  obtain ⟨b, q, hq⟩ := exists_T_pow g
166	  have key : Polynomial.toLaurent (p * q) = Polynomial.toLaurent (Polynomial.X ^ (a + b)) := by
167	    rw [map_mul, hp, hq]
168	    rw [show (f * T (a : ℤ)) * (g * T (b : ℤ)) = (f * g) * T ((a : ℤ) + b) by
169	      rw [T_add]; ring]
170	    rw [hg, one_mul]
171	    simp
172	  have hpq : p * q = Polynomial.X ^ (a + b) := toLaurent_injective key
173	  obtain ⟨i, _, u, hu⟩ := (dvd_prime_pow Polynomial.prime_X (a + b)).mp ⟨q, hpq.symm⟩
174	  obtain ⟨c, hc, hcu⟩ := Polynomial.isUnit_iff.mp (Units.isUnit u⁻¹)
175	  have hpX : p = Polynomial.C c * Polynomial.X ^ i := by
176	    have hpu : p = Polynomial.X ^ i * (↑u⁻¹ : Polynomial R) := by rw [← hu, mul_assoc]; simp
177	    rw [hpu, hcu, mul_comm]
178	  refine ⟨c, (i : ℤ) - a, hc, ?_⟩
179	  have hf' : f = Polynomial.toLaurent p * T (-(a : ℤ)) := by
180	    rw [hp, mul_assoc, ← T_add]; simp
181	  rw [hf', hpX, map_mul, toLaurent_C, map_pow, toLaurent_X, mul_assoc, T_pow, ← T_add,
182	    show ((i : ℤ) * 1 + -(a : ℤ)) = (i : ℤ) - a by ring]
183	
184	/-- **The unit classification of `R[T;T⁻¹]` over a domain**, as an iff. -/
185	theorem isUnit_iff_C_mul_T {f : LaurentPolynomial R} :
186	    IsUnit f ↔ ∃ (c : R) (n : ℤ), IsUnit c ∧ f = LaurentPolynomial.C c * T n := by
187	  refine ⟨exists_eq_C_mul_T_of_isUnit, ?_⟩
188	  rintro ⟨c, n, hc, rfl⟩
189	  exact isUnit_C_mul_T hc n
190	
191	/-! ## The unit group as a product
192	
193	The classification packaged as a group isomorphism `Rˣ × ℤ ≃* (R[T;T⁻¹])ˣ`.  This is the form
194	the Picard computation wants: the two chart unit groups of `ℙ¹` both land in the constants
195	(units of `k[t]` are constants by `Polynomial.isUnit_iff`), so the two-cover Čech `Ȟ¹` of units
196	is this group modulo `Rˣ` — the `ℤ` factor, and nothing else. -/
197	
198	/-- `T n` as a unit. -/
199	noncomputable def tUnit (n : ℤ) : (LaurentPolynomial R)ˣ := (isUnit_T n).unit
200	
201	omit [IsDomain R] in
202	@[simp]
203	theorem tUnit_coe (n : ℤ) : ((tUnit (R := R) n : (LaurentPolynomial R)ˣ)
204	    : LaurentPolynomial R) = T n := rfl
205	
206	/-- The homomorphism `Rˣ × ℤ →* (R[T;T⁻¹])ˣ` sending `(c, n)` to `C c * T n`.  Over any
207	commutative ring; the domain hypothesis is only needed for surjectivity. -/
208	noncomputable def unitsHom :
209	    Rˣ × Multiplicative ℤ →* (LaurentPolynomial R)ˣ where
210	  toFun p := (Units.map (LaurentPolynomial.C : R →+* LaurentPolynomial R).toMonoidHom p.1)
211	      * tUnit (Multiplicative.toAdd p.2)
212	  map_one' := Units.ext (by
213	    change (LaurentPolynomial.C (1 : R)) * T (0 : ℤ) = 1
214	    rw [map_one, T_zero, one_mul])
215	  map_mul' a b := Units.ext (by
216	    change LaurentPolynomial.C ((a.1 * b.1 : Rˣ) : R) * T (Multiplicative.toAdd (a.2 * b.2))
217	      = (LaurentPolynomial.C (a.1 : R) * T (Multiplicative.toAdd a.2))
218	        * (LaurentPolynomial.C (b.1 : R) * T (Multiplicative.toAdd b.2))
219	    push_cast
220	    have hT : (T (Multiplicative.toAdd (a.2 * b.2)) : LaurentPolynomial R)
221	        = T (Multiplicative.toAdd a.2) * T (Multiplicative.toAdd b.2) := by
222	      rw [← T_add]; rfl
223	    rw [map_mul, hT]
224	    ring)
225	
226	omit [IsDomain R] in
227	@[simp]
228	theorem unitsHom_coe (p : Rˣ × Multiplicative ℤ) :
229	    ((unitsHom p : (LaurentPolynomial R)ˣ) : LaurentPolynomial R)
230	      = LaurentPolynomial.C (p.1 : R) * T (Multiplicative.toAdd p.2) :=
231	  rfl
232	
233	omit [IsDomain R] in
234	/-- The coefficient of a Laurent monomial is determined once the exponent is.  Companion to
235	`exp_unique`, and like it needs no domain hypothesis (the `omit` is the measurement). -/
236	theorem coeff_unique {c d : R} {n : ℤ}
237	    (h : (LaurentPolynomial.C c * T n : LaurentPolynomial R)
238	      = LaurentPolynomial.C d * T n) : c = d := by
239	  have h1 := congrArg (fun f : LaurentPolynomial R => f n) h
240	  simp only [← LaurentPolynomial.single_eq_C_mul_T] at h1
241	  rw [show (AddMonoidAlgebra.single n c : LaurentPolynomial R) = Finsupp.single n c from rfl,
242	      show (AddMonoidAlgebra.single n d : LaurentPolynomial R) = Finsupp.single n d from rfl,
243	      Finsupp.single_eq_same, Finsupp.single_eq_same] at h1
244	  exact h1
245	
246	theorem unitsHom_surjective : Function.Surjective (unitsHom (R := R)) := by
247	  intro u
248	  obtain ⟨c, n, hc, hu⟩ := exists_eq_C_mul_T_of_isUnit u.isUnit
249	  refine ⟨(hc.unit, Multiplicative.ofAdd n), Units.ext ?_⟩
250	  rw [unitsHom_coe, hu]
251	  simp
252	
253	theorem unitsHom_injective : Function.Injective (unitsHom (R := R)) := by
254	  intro p q hpq
255	  have h : LaurentPolynomial.C (p.1 : R) * T (Multiplicative.toAdd p.2)
256	      = LaurentPolynomial.C (q.1 : R) * T (Multiplicative.toAdd q.2) :=
257	    congrArg (fun v : (LaurentPolynomial R)ˣ => (v : LaurentPolynomial R)) hpq
258	  have hne : (p.1 : R) ≠ 0 := p.1.ne_zero
259	  have hexp : Multiplicative.toAdd p.2 = Multiplicative.toAdd q.2 := exp_unique hne h
260	  have hsnd : p.2 = q.2 := Multiplicative.toAdd.injective hexp
261	  have hsame : LaurentPolynomial.C (p.1 : R) * T (Multiplicative.toAdd p.2)
262	      = LaurentPolynomial.C (q.1 : R) * T (Multiplicative.toAdd p.2) := by
263	    rw [h, hexp]
264	  exact Prod.ext (Units.ext (coeff_unique hsame)) hsnd
265	
266	/-- **`(R[T;T⁻¹])ˣ ≅ Rˣ × ℤ`** over a domain.  The `ℤ` is the exponent and the `Rˣ` is the
267	coefficient; `exp_unique` and `coeff_unique` are the two halves of injectivity, and the
268	classification is surjectivity. -/
269	noncomputable def unitsEquiv : Rˣ × Multiplicative ℤ ≃* (LaurentPolynomial R)ˣ :=
270	  MulEquiv.ofBijective unitsHom ⟨unitsHom_injective, unitsHom_surjective⟩
271	
272	end LaurentPolynomial

10	# The relative Picard functor of a curve
11	
12	For a scheme `C` over a field `k` (an object of `Over (Spec k)`) this file defines the
13	relative Picard functor of Grothendieck–Kleiman:
14	$$\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}(T) \;=\; \operatorname{Pic}(C \times_k T)\,/\,
15	  \operatorname{Pic}(T),$$
16	line-bundle classes on `C ⊗ T` modulo classes pulled back from the test object `T`
17	along the second projection. The quotient — never the absolute `Pic(C ⊗ T)`, which is
18	not even a separated presheaf in any useful sense — is the functor that étale
19	sheafification and the representability theorem consume.
20	
21	Products are the cartesian-monoidal product of `Over (Spec k)` (chosen pullbacks of
22	schemes): `C ⊗ T`, projection `snd C T`, whiskering `C ◁ g`, matching the vocabulary
23	of the challenge statement file.
24	
25	## Main declarations
26	
27	* `AlgebraicGeometry.picFromBase C T`: the subgroup of `(C ⊗ T).left.CechPic` of classes
28	  pulled back from `T` along the second projection.
29	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPic C T`: the relative Picard group, the quotient by
30	  `picFromBase C T`, a `CommGroup`; `relPicMk` is the projection, with
31	  `relPicMk_eq_relPicMk_iff` the exact coset relation (a genuine range condition, no
32	  choice, no `Nonempty (≅)`).
33	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPicMap C g`: restriction along `g : T' ⟶ T`, descended from
34	  pullback of Čech classes along `C ◁ g`.
35	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPicFunctor C`: the relative Picard functor
36	  `(Over (Spec k))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat`.
37	-/

43	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory Opposite
44	open AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme (CechPic)

46	namespace AlgebraicGeometry

48	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
49	
50	noncomputable section
51	
52	/-- The subgroup of Picard classes on `C ⊗ T` pulled back from the test object `T`
53	along the second projection. The relative Picard group is the quotient by it. -/
54	def picFromBase (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Subgroup ((C ⊗ T).left.CechPic) :=
55	  (CechPic.map (snd C T).left).range
56	
57	lemma mem_picFromBase_iff {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {L : (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic} :
58	    L ∈ picFromBase C T ↔ ∃ N : T.left.CechPic, CechPic.map (snd C T).left N = L :=
59	  Iff.rfl
60	
61	/-- The relative Picard group of `C/k` at a test object `T`: Picard classes on `C ⊗ T`
62	modulo classes pulled back from `T`. -/
63	def relPic (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Type u :=
64	  (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic ⧸ picFromBase C T
65	
66	noncomputable instance (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : CommGroup (relPic C T) :=
67	  QuotientGroup.Quotient.commGroup (picFromBase C T)
68	
69	/-- The projection from Picard classes on `C ⊗ T` to the relative Picard group. -/
70	noncomputable def relPicMk (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) :
71	    (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic →* relPic C T :=
72	  QuotientGroup.mk' (picFromBase C T)
73	
74	lemma relPicMk_surjective (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) :
75	    Function.Surjective (relPicMk C T) :=
76	  QuotientGroup.mk'_surjective (picFromBase C T)
77	
78	/-- The exact coset relation: two Picard classes on `C ⊗ T` have equal image in the
79	relative Picard group iff their ratio is pulled back from `T`. -/
80	lemma relPicMk_eq_relPicMk_iff {T : Over (Spec (.of k))}
81	    {L L' : (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic} :
82	    relPicMk C T L = relPicMk C T L' ↔ L / L' ∈ picFromBase C T :=
83	  QuotientGroup.eq_iff_div_mem
84	
85	@[elab_as_elim]
86	theorem relPic.ind {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {motive : relPic C T → Prop}
87	    (mk : ∀ L : (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic, motive (relPicMk C T L)) (x : relPic C T) :
88	    motive x :=
89	  QuotientGroup.induction_on x mk

91	variable {T T' T'' : Over (Spec (.of k))}
92	
93	/-- Pullback of Čech Picard classes along `C ◁ g` sends classes from `T` to classes
94	from `T'`: the well-definedness of `relPicMap` on the `H_T`-cosets. -/
95	lemma picFromBase_le_comap (g : T' ⟶ T) :
96	    picFromBase C T ≤ (picFromBase C T').comap (CechPic.map (C ◁ g).left) := by
97	  rintro _ ⟨N, rfl⟩
98	  refine ⟨CechPic.map g.left N, ?_⟩
99	  show CechPic.map (snd C T').left (CechPic.map g.left N)
100	      = CechPic.map (C ◁ g).left (CechPic.map (snd C T).left N)
101	  rw [← MonoidHom.comp_apply, ← MonoidHom.comp_apply, ← Scheme.CechPic.map_comp,
102	    ← Scheme.CechPic.map_comp, ← Over.comp_left, ← Over.comp_left, whiskerLeft_snd]
103	
104	/-- Restriction of relative Picard classes along `g : T' ⟶ T`: pull back along
105	`C ◁ g` and descend to the quotients. -/
106	noncomputable def relPicMap (g : T' ⟶ T) : relPic C T →* relPic C T' :=
107	  QuotientGroup.map (picFromBase C T) (picFromBase C T')
108	    (CechPic.map (C ◁ g).left) (picFromBase_le_comap C g)
109	
110	@[simp]
111	lemma relPicMap_mk (g : T' ⟶ T) (L : (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic) :
112	    relPicMap C g (relPicMk C T L) = relPicMk C T' (CechPic.map (C ◁ g).left L) :=
113	  QuotientGroup.map_mk' _ _ _ _ L
114	
115	lemma relPicMap_id (x : relPic C T) : relPicMap C (𝟙 T) x = x := by
116	  induction x using relPic.ind with
117	  | mk L =>
118	    rw [relPicMap_mk, MonoidalCategory.whiskerLeft_id, Over.id_left,
119	      Scheme.CechPic.map_id]
120	    rfl
121	
122	lemma relPicMap_comp (g : T' ⟶ T) (h : T'' ⟶ T') (x : relPic C T) :
123	    relPicMap C (h ≫ g) x = relPicMap C h (relPicMap C g x) := by
124	  induction x using relPic.ind with
125	  | mk L =>
126	    rw [relPicMap_mk, relPicMap_mk, relPicMap_mk]
127	    refine congrArg (relPicMk C T'') ?_
128	    rw [← MonoidHom.comp_apply, ← Scheme.CechPic.map_comp, ← Over.comp_left,
129	      ← MonoidalCategory.whiskerLeft_comp]
130	
131	/-- The relative Picard functor `T ↦ Pic(C ⊗ T)/Pic(T)` of Grothendieck–Kleiman, as a
132	presheaf of commutative groups on `Over (Spec k)`. -/
133	noncomputable def relPicFunctor : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat.{u} where
134	  obj T := CommGrpCat.of (relPic C T.unop)
135	  map g := CommGrpCat.ofHom (relPicMap C g.unop)
136	  map_id T := by
137	    ext x
138	    exact relPicMap_id C x
139	  map_comp g h := by
140	    ext x
141	    exact relPicMap_comp C g.unop h.unop x
142	
143	@[simp]
144	lemma relPicFunctor_obj (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ) :
145	    (relPicFunctor C).obj T = CommGrpCat.of (relPic C T.unop) :=
146	  rfl
147	
148	@[simp]
149	lemma relPicFunctor_map {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ} (g : T ⟶ T')
150	    (x : relPic C T.unop) :
151	    (relPicFunctor C).map g x = relPicMap C g.unop x :=
152	  rfl

154	/-! ## Naturality in the curve -/
155	
156	variable {C} {C' C'' : Over (Spec (.of k))}
157	
158	/-- Pullback of Čech classes along `g ▷ T` sends classes pulled back from `T` to classes
159	pulled back from `T`: well-definedness of the curve-direction map on the `H_T`-cosets. -/
160	lemma picFromBase_le_comap_whiskerRight (g : C' ⟶ C) (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) :
161	    picFromBase C T ≤ (picFromBase C' T).comap (CechPic.map (g ▷ T).left) := by
162	  rintro _ ⟨N, rfl⟩
163	  refine ⟨N, ?_⟩
164	  show CechPic.map (snd C' T).left N
165	      = CechPic.map (g ▷ T).left (CechPic.map (snd C T).left N)
166	  rw [← MonoidHom.comp_apply, ← Scheme.CechPic.map_comp, ← Over.comp_left,
167	    whiskerRight_snd]
168	
169	/-- Restriction of relative Picard classes along a morphism of curves `g : C' ⟶ C`,
170	at a fixed test object: pull back along `g ▷ T` and descend to the quotients. -/
171	noncomputable def relPicMapCurveApp (g : C' ⟶ C) (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) :
172	    relPic C T →* relPic C' T :=
173	  QuotientGroup.map (picFromBase C T) (picFromBase C' T)
174	    (CechPic.map (g ▷ T).left) (picFromBase_le_comap_whiskerRight g T)
175	
176	@[simp]
177	lemma relPicMapCurveApp_mk (g : C' ⟶ C) (T : Over (Spec (.of k)))
178	    (L : (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic) :
179	    relPicMapCurveApp g T (relPicMk C T L)
180	      = relPicMk C' T (CechPic.map (g ▷ T).left L) :=
181	  QuotientGroup.map_mk' _ _ _ _ L
182	
183	/-- Naturality of the relative Picard functor in the curve: a morphism of curves
184	`g : C' ⟶ C` induces a natural transformation `Pic_{C/k} ⟶ Pic_{C'/k}`. -/
185	noncomputable def relPicMapCurve (g : C' ⟶ C) :
186	    relPicFunctor C ⟶ relPicFunctor C' where
187	  app T := CommGrpCat.ofHom (relPicMapCurveApp g T.unop)
188	  naturality T T' t := by
189	    ext x
190	    induction x using relPic.ind with
191	    | mk L =>
192	      show relPicMapCurveApp g T'.unop (relPicMap C t.unop (relPicMk C T.unop L))
193	          = relPicMap C' t.unop (relPicMapCurveApp g T.unop (relPicMk C T.unop L))
194	      rw [relPicMap_mk, relPicMapCurveApp_mk, relPicMapCurveApp_mk, relPicMap_mk]
195	      refine congrArg (relPicMk C' T'.unop) ?_
196	      rw [← MonoidHom.comp_apply, ← MonoidHom.comp_apply, ← Scheme.CechPic.map_comp,
197	        ← Scheme.CechPic.map_comp, ← Over.comp_left, ← Over.comp_left, whisker_exchange]
198	
199	@[simp]
200	lemma relPicMapCurve_app_mk (g : C' ⟶ C) (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ)
201	    (L : (C ⊗ T.unop).left.CechPic) :
202	    (relPicMapCurve g).app T (relPicMk C T.unop L)
203	      = relPicMk C' T.unop (CechPic.map (g ▷ T.unop).left L) :=
204	  relPicMapCurveApp_mk g T.unop L
205	
206	/-- The curve-direction maps are strictly functorial: the identity morphism induces the
207	identity transformation. -/
208	lemma relPicMapCurve_id : relPicMapCurve (𝟙 C) = 𝟙 (relPicFunctor C) := by
209	  ext T x
210	  induction x using relPic.ind with
211	  | mk L =>
212	    show relPicMapCurveApp (𝟙 C) T.unop (relPicMk C T.unop L) = relPicMk C T.unop L
213	    rw [relPicMapCurveApp_mk, MonoidalCategory.id_whiskerRight, Over.id_left,
214	      Scheme.CechPic.map_id]
215	    rfl
216	
217	/-- The curve-direction maps are strictly functorial: composition of curve morphisms
218	goes to composition of the induced transformations (contravariantly). -/
219	lemma relPicMapCurve_comp (g' : C'' ⟶ C') (g : C' ⟶ C) :
220	    relPicMapCurve (g' ≫ g) = relPicMapCurve g ≫ relPicMapCurve g' := by
221	  ext T x
222	  induction x using relPic.ind with
223	  | mk L =>
224	    show relPicMapCurveApp (g' ≫ g) T.unop (relPicMk C T.unop L)
225	        = relPicMapCurveApp g' T.unop (relPicMapCurveApp g T.unop (relPicMk C T.unop L))
226	    rw [relPicMapCurveApp_mk, relPicMapCurveApp_mk, relPicMapCurveApp_mk]
227	    refine congrArg (relPicMk C'' T.unop) ?_
228	    rw [← MonoidHom.comp_apply, ← Scheme.CechPic.map_comp, ← Over.comp_left,
229	      ← MonoidalCategory.comp_whiskerRight]
230	
231	end

9	/-!
10	# THE ℙ¹ TWO-CHART COBOUNDARY SUBGROUP OVER A DOMAIN IS EXACTLY THE CONSTANTS
11	
12	`Picard/TwoChartCechPicTrivial.lean` reduces triviality of a chart-trivial Picard class on a
13	two-chart cover to the purely algebraic question *are the overlap units all coboundaries?*.  This
14	file answers that question for the pinned ℙ¹ chart data — overlap ring `A[t,t⁻¹]`, chart rings
15	`A[t]` and `A[t⁻¹]` — over a **domain** `A`, in both directions:
16	
17	> a Laurent unit is a coboundary **iff** it is `C c` for a unit `c` of `A`.
18	
19	## Read this before using it: the answer is NO, and that is the correct answer
20	
21	The criterion of the previous file asks for *every* overlap unit to be a coboundary.  Over a
22	domain that is **false**, and this file is what proves it false: `T 1 = t` is a unit of
23	`A[t,t⁻¹]` and is *not* a coboundary, because `t` is a unit of neither chart ring
24	(`Polynomial.isUnit_iff`: a unit of `A[t]` over a domain is a constant).
25	
26	That is not an obstruction to the route — it is the statement that
27	
28	```
29	Pic(ℙ¹_A)  =  A[t,t⁻¹]ˣ ⧸ (A[t]ˣ · A[t⁻¹]ˣ)  =  ℤ,
30	```
31	
32	the classical computation, with the class of `t` generating.  The consequence for the
33	representability route is the useful one, and it is a *sharpening* rather than a defeat: the
34	hypothesis that must be supplied is not "all overlap units are coboundaries" but "the overlap
35	unit presenting **this** class has exponent zero" — i.e. exactly a degree-zero condition, which
36	is what `pic0Subgroup` cuts out in the first place.  A lane pricing the ring case should price
37	that, not the false universal form.
38	
39	## Where `IsDomain` is used, and where it is not
40	
41	* the **forward** direction (a coboundary is a constant) uses it, through
42	  `Polynomial.isUnit_iff` on each chart — over a general ring `A[t]` has non-constant units
43	  (`1 + εt` with `ε² = 0`) and the direction genuinely fails;
44	* the **converse** (a constant unit is a coboundary) uses **no** hypothesis on `A`: `C c` is the
45	  left chart's image of the polynomial unit `C c`.  The `omit` marker records that.
46	
47	`Algebra/LaurentUnits.lean` already proves the necessity of `IsDomain` for the Laurent unit
48	classification as a theorem rather than a remark; this file is the two-chart-cohomological
49	consequence of that classification.
50	
51	## Main declarations
52	
53	* `AlgebraicGeometry.rightChart` — the second chart map `A[t] → A[t,t⁻¹]`, `t ↦ T (-1)`.  The
54	  two charts of ℙ¹ are both polynomial rings; they differ by which of `t, t⁻¹` they send `X` to.
55	* `AlgebraicGeometry.C_unit_mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits` — a constant unit is a coboundary, over
56	  any commutative ring.
57	* `AlgebraicGeometry.eq_C_of_mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits` — over a domain, a coboundary is a
58	  constant unit.
59	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits_iff` — the two together, as an `iff`.
60	* `AlgebraicGeometry.not_tUnit_mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits` — `t` is **not** a coboundary over a
61	  nontrivial domain: the generator of `Pic(ℙ¹_A) = ℤ`, and the refutation of the universal form
62	  of the criterion's hypothesis.
63	-/
64	
65	set_option autoImplicit false
66	
67	universe u
68	
69	open CategoryTheory
70	
71	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
72	
73	variable {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
74	
75	/-- The second ℙ¹ chart map `A[t] → A[t,t⁻¹]`, sending the coordinate to `t⁻¹`.  The first is
76	mathlib's `Polynomial.toLaurent` (`X ↦ T 1`); both chart rings are polynomial rings, and the
77	cover is recorded by *which* Laurent monomial the coordinate goes to. -/
78	noncomputable def rightChart (A : Type u) [CommRing A] :
79	    Polynomial A →+* LaurentPolynomial A :=
80	  Polynomial.eval₂RingHom LaurentPolynomial.C (LaurentPolynomial.T (-1))
81	
82	@[simp]
83	lemma rightChart_X : (rightChart A) Polynomial.X = LaurentPolynomial.T (-1) := by
84	  simp [rightChart]
85	
86	@[simp]
87	lemma rightChart_C (c : A) : (rightChart A) (Polynomial.C c) = LaurentPolynomial.C c := by
88	  simp [rightChart]
89	
90	/-- The coboundary subgroup of the ℙ¹ overlap units: products of images of the two chart unit
91	groups.  Abbreviation for the `TruncExpCech` subgroup at the two chart maps. -/
92	noncomputable abbrev laurentCoboundaryUnits (A : Type u) [CommRing A] :
93	    Subgroup (LaurentPolynomial A)ˣ :=
94	  TruncExpCech.cechCoboundaryUnits
95	    (Polynomial.toLaurent : Polynomial A →+* LaurentPolynomial A) (rightChart A)
96	
97	/-- **A constant unit is a coboundary** — no hypothesis on `A`.
98	
99	`LaurentPolynomial.C c` is the left chart's image of the polynomial unit `Polynomial.C c`. -/
100	theorem C_unit_mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits (c : Aˣ) :
101	    (Units.map (LaurentPolynomial.C : A →+* LaurentPolynomial A).toMonoidHom c)
102	      ∈ laurentCoboundaryUnits A := by
103	  have h : Units.map (LaurentPolynomial.C : A →+* LaurentPolynomial A).toMonoidHom c
104	      = Units.map (Polynomial.toLaurent : Polynomial A →+* LaurentPolynomial A).toMonoidHom
105	          (Units.map (Polynomial.C : A →+* Polynomial A).toMonoidHom c) := by
106	    ext; simp
107	  rw [h]
108	  exact TruncExpCech.unitsMap_mem_cechCoboundaryUnits_left _ _ _
109	
110	/-- **Over a domain, a coboundary is a constant unit.**
111	
112	Both chart unit groups consist of constants (`Polynomial.isUnit_iff`, which needs `IsDomain`),
113	and both chart maps send `Polynomial.C c` to `LaurentPolynomial.C c`, so a product of chart
114	images is `C` of the product.
115	
116	This is the direction that fails over a general ring: `1 + εt` is a unit of `A[t]` whenever
117	`ε² = 0`, so `A[t]ˣ` is bigger than the constants there. -/
118	theorem eq_C_of_mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits [IsDomain A] {u : (LaurentPolynomial A)ˣ}
119	    (hu : u ∈ laurentCoboundaryUnits A) :
120	    ∃ c : A, IsUnit c ∧ (u : LaurentPolynomial A) = LaurentPolynomial.C c := by
121	  obtain ⟨v, w, hvw⟩ := TruncExpCech.mem_cechCoboundaryUnits.mp hu
122	  obtain ⟨cv, hcv, hv⟩ := Polynomial.isUnit_iff.mp v.isUnit
123	  obtain ⟨cw, hcw, hw⟩ := Polynomial.isUnit_iff.mp w.isUnit
124	  refine ⟨cv * cw, hcv.mul hcw, ?_⟩
125	  rw [← hvw]
126	  show Polynomial.toLaurent (v : Polynomial A) * (rightChart A) (w : Polynomial A)
127	    = LaurentPolynomial.C (cv * cw)
128	  rw [← hv, ← hw]
129	  simp [rightChart, map_mul]
130	
131	/-- **THE CHARACTERIZATION**: over a domain, the coboundary subgroup is exactly the constants.
132	
133	So the two-chart Čech Picard group of `ℙ¹_A` is the Laurent units modulo the constants, which by
134	`LaurentPolynomial.unitsEquiv` (`Aˣ × ℤ`) is `ℤ`. -/
135	theorem mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits_iff [IsDomain A] {u : (LaurentPolynomial A)ˣ} :
136	    u ∈ laurentCoboundaryUnits A
137	      ↔ ∃ c : A, IsUnit c ∧ (u : LaurentPolynomial A) = LaurentPolynomial.C c := by
138	  refine ⟨eq_C_of_mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits, ?_⟩
139	  rintro ⟨c, hc, hu⟩
140	  obtain ⟨cu, rfl⟩ := hc
141	  have h : u = Units.map (LaurentPolynomial.C : A →+* LaurentPolynomial A).toMonoidHom cu :=
142	    Units.ext hu
143	  rw [h]
144	  exact C_unit_mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits cu
145	
146	/-- **`t` IS NOT A COBOUNDARY** over a nontrivial domain — the generator of
147	`Pic(ℙ¹_A) = ℤ`, and the refutation of the *universal* form of the criterion's hypothesis in
148	`Picard/TwoChartCechPicTrivial.lean`.
149	
150	If it were, it would be a constant by `eq_C_of_mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits`; but `T 1` has its
151	support in degree `1`, and comparing coefficients at `0` gives `0 = c` while at `1` gives
152	`1 = 0`.
153	
154	Recorded as a theorem rather than a remark because the previous file's criterion asks for *every*
155	overlap unit to be a coboundary, and a consumer must know that that hypothesis is FALSE here — so
156	the thing to supply is a degree-zero condition on the presenting unit, not the universal form. -/
157	theorem not_tUnit_mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits [IsDomain A] [Nontrivial A] :
158	    LaurentPolynomial.tUnit (R := A) 1 ∉ laurentCoboundaryUnits A := by
159	  intro hmem
160	  obtain ⟨c, _, hc⟩ := eq_C_of_mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits hmem
161	  rw [LaurentPolynomial.tUnit_coe] at hc
162	  have h1 : (LaurentPolynomial.T (1 : ℤ) : LaurentPolynomial A) 1 = 1 := by
163	    simp [LaurentPolynomial.T]
164	  have h2 : (LaurentPolynomial.C c : LaurentPolynomial A) 1 = 0 := by
165	    simp [LaurentPolynomial.C, LaurentPolynomial.single_eq_C]
166	  rw [hc, h2] at h1
167	  exact one_ne_zero h1.symm

9	/-!
10	# A CHART-TRIVIAL PICARD CLASS IS TRIVIAL WHEN THE OVERLAP UNITS ARE ALL COBOUNDARIES
11	
12	For a scheme `X` with two opens `V₀ ⊔ V₁ = ⊤`, the Wave-5 tangent lane built both halves of

42	`CechPic ((C ⊗ overSpec k K).left)` — the Čech Picard group of the curve base-changed to `K`.
43	So the field-point content of the vanishing is a statement about `ℙ¹_K` for every `K`, and a
44	computation over `k` alone does not touch it.

46	## The composite, and where each input comes from

48	`genus (baseChangeBundle C K) = genus C` is base-field invariance of the genus
49	(`Cohomology/H1BaseFieldInvariance.lean:373`), and `χ(𝒪) = 1 - genus`

    {U V : Set α} (hVo : IsOpen V) (hU : IsIrreducible U) (hV : IsIrreducible V)
    (hUV : (U ∩ V).Nonempty) (hcov : ∀ x : α, x ∈ U ∨ x ∈ V) :

  -- common point `w`.  So `u` and `v` both meet `V`, and `V`'s irreducibility finishes.

      (U ∩ (u' ∩ V)).Nonempty := fun {u'} hu' {c} hcu' hcU =>

88	  no section and no curve hypothesis, for every class in the range of `relPicToPicEt`.  So the
89	  seam is not the obstruction it was priced as; `presentation_of_relPicToPicEt` below is that
90	  observation made usable, and `rigidEngine_of_relPicToPicEt` fires the engine with the
91	  presentation binder **eliminated** for such classes.
92	
93	  What is genuinely missing is therefore **surjectivity of `relPicToPicEt` onto `picEt`** — that
94	  every étale-plus class over a ring comes from a relative Picard class — which is a different
95	  statement about a different map, and is what a lane wanting these conclusions at an
96	  *arbitrary* degree-zero class should target.  `Pic0ChartPlusFibreProducer.lean:199` calls
97	  membership in that range "honesty" and treats it as a real condition, which is consistent.
98	* **Genus `0` only.**  At positive genus the fibre classes are not trivial.
99	
100	## Main declarations
101	
102	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relCurveMap_eq_whiskerLeft_residueField` — the `I-0144` spelling bridge.
103	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_datum_relPicMk_eq` / `exists_datum_pic0_presentation` — the datum in
104	  the presentation binder is produced, not assumed, at every test ring.
105	* `AlgebraicGeometry.BasicOpenCocycleDatum.htriv_of_pic0` — **the discharge**: the engine's
106	  fibrewise binder, from a cocycle-presented `pic⁰` class.
107	* `AlgebraicGeometry.BasicOpenCocycleDatum.rigidEngine_of_pic0` — the engine's three
108	  conclusions with no fibrewise hypothesis.
109	* `AlgebraicGeometry.BasicOpenCocycleDatum.rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one_of_pic0` —
110	  **`π_*L` invertible** from a `pic⁰` membership.
111	* `AlgebraicGeometry.P1.rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one_of_pic0` — non-vacuity at `ℙ¹` over an
112	  arbitrary field.
113	-/

131	/-! ## The spelling bridge (`I-0144`) -/
132	
133	/-- **The two `overSpecMap`s agree at a residue field.**
134	
135	`overSpecMap B κ(p)` (`Cohomology/RelativeSectionsLinear.lean:147`) is built from the
136	`algebraMap`; `Over.overSpecMap φ` (`Picard/RelPicAlgebra.lean:44`) from an arbitrary
137	`k`-algebra map.  These are two independent definitions of the same morphism in different
138	namespaces — the duplicate pair filed as `I-0144` — and at the canonical map
139	`(Algebra.ofId B κ(p)).restrictScalars k` they are definitionally equal.
140	
141	Stated because the engine's base-change lemmas live on the first spelling and the degree seam
142	on the second, so no composition of the two is possible without it. -/
143	theorem relCurveMap_eq_whiskerLeft_residueField (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
144	    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] (p : PrimeSpectrum B) :
145	    relCurveMap C B p.asIdeal.ResidueField
146	      = (C ◁ Over.overSpecMap
147	          ((Algebra.ofId B p.asIdeal.ResidueField).restrictScalars k)).left :=
148	  rfl

150	/-! ## The datum in the presentation binder is not a real constraint -/
151	
152	/-- **Every relative Picard class over a test ring is presented by a cocycle datum.**
153	
154	`relPicMk` is surjective (`RelPic.lean:75`) and `exists_cechPicClass_eq`
155	(`Cohomology/GluedSheafExtraction.lean:301`) turns the resulting Čech class into a
156	`BasicOpenCocycleDatum` with the same class, at **every** `k`-algebra `B`.
157	
158	This is what makes the presentation binder of the theorems below a condition on the *class*
159	rather than on a choice of datum: a `pic⁰` class that is `PicEtAff.unit` of some relative class
160	at all is presented by some datum, and `exists_datum_pic0_presentation` extracts it. -/
161	theorem exists_datum_relPicMk_eq (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
162	    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite π]
163	    (z : relPic C (overSpec k B)) :
164	    ∃ D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π, relPicMk C (overSpec k B) D.cechPicClass = z := by
165	  obtain ⟨L, hL⟩ := relPicMk_surjective C (overSpec k B) z
166	  obtain ⟨D, hD⟩ := BasicOpenCocycleDatum.exists_cechPicClass_eq (π := π) L
167	  exact ⟨D, by rw [hD, hL]⟩
168	
169	/-- **The presentation binder, in its weakest form**: if the affine collapse of `lam` is
170	`PicEtAff.unit` of *any* relative class, then it is `PicEtAff.unit` of `relPicMk` of some
171	datum's Čech class — which is the hypothesis the theorems below take.
172	
173	So those theorems do not secretly quantify over a lucky datum: the datum is produced, and the
174	surviving hypothesis is the `picEtAffineEquiv`/`unit` seam on `lam` alone. -/
175	theorem exists_datum_pic0_presentation (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
176	    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite π]
177	    (lam : picEt C (overSpec k B))
178	    (h : ∃ z : relPic C (overSpec k B), picEtAffineEquiv C B lam = PicEtAff.unit C B z) :
179	    ∃ D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π,
180	      picEtAffineEquiv C B lam
181	        = PicEtAff.unit C B (relPicMk C (overSpec k B) D.cechPicClass) := by
182	  obtain ⟨z, hz⟩ := h
183	  obtain ⟨D, hD⟩ := exists_datum_relPicMk_eq C B π z
184	  exact ⟨D, by rw [hz, hD]⟩

186	namespace BasicOpenCocycleDatum

188	/-! ## The fibrewise binder, discharged -/
189	
190	/-- **THE DISCHARGE**: the engine's fibrewise binder holds for a cocycle-presented `pic⁰`
191	class, at genus `0`.
192	
193	Composition of three landed steps and the bridge above:
194	`cechPicClass_baseChange` moves the fibre class onto `Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap …)`;
195	the bridge rewrites that as the whiskering the degree seam speaks about;
196	`classDeg_fibre_eq_zero_of_cocyclePresented` gives `classDeg κ(p) = 0` from the membership;
197	and the engine's `fibre_cechPicClass_eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero` converts degree `0` to
198	triviality at genus `0`.
199	
200	The five fibre instances are installed by hand — they do not synthesize through the `relCurve`
201	`def` barrier, exactly as `Pic0RingDatumEngine` records. -/
202	theorem htriv_of_pic0 (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π) (hg : genus C = 0)
203	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k B))
204	    (h : picEtAffineEquiv C B (lam : picEt C (overSpec k B))
205	      = PicEtAff.unit C B (relPicMk C (overSpec k B) D.cechPicClass))
206	    (p : PrimeSpectrum B) :
207	    (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).cechPicClass = 1 := by
208	  haveI : IsIntegral (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :=
209	    instIsIntegralBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
210	  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
211	      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :=
212	    instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
213	  haveI : QuasiCompact
214	      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :=
215	    instQuasiCompactBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
216	  haveI : Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField (Sheaf.HModule
217	      ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 0) :=
218	    instModuleFiniteHModuleZeroBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
219	  haveI : Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField (Sheaf.HModule
220	      ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 1) :=
221	    instModuleFiniteHModuleOneBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
222	  refine D.fibre_cechPicClass_eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero hg p ?_
223	  rw [D.cechPicClass_baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField,
224	    relCurveMap_eq_whiskerLeft_residueField C B p]
225	  exact classDeg_fibre_eq_zero_of_cocyclePresented C lam D.cechPicClass h _
226	
227	/-! ## The engine, with no fibrewise hypothesis -/
228	
229	/-- **The rigid engine from a `pic⁰` membership**: `H¹(C_B, F_D) = 0` and `H⁰(C_B, F_D)` finite
230	projective over `B`, for a cocycle-presented degree-zero class at genus `0`.
231	
232	No fibrewise clause appears in the statement: the hypotheses are the membership, its
233	presentation, and the engine's own `IsNoetherianRing B`. -/
234	theorem rigidEngine_of_pic0 (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π) [IsNoetherianRing B]
235	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom) (hg : genus C = 0)
236	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k B))
237	    (h : picEtAffineEquiv C B (lam : picEt C (overSpec k B))
238	      = PicEtAff.unit C B (relPicMk C (overSpec k B) D.cechPicClass)) :
239	    Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 1) ∧
240	      Module.Finite B (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0) ∧
241	      Module.Projective B (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0) :=
242	  D.rigidEngine_of_genus_zero hπ hg (D.htriv_of_pic0 hg lam h)
243	
244	/-- **`π_*L` IS INVERTIBLE, FROM A `pic⁰` MEMBERSHIP** — the stalk rank of `H⁰` is `1` at every
245	prime of the test ring, for a cocycle-presented degree-zero class at genus `0`.
246	
247	This is the cohomological output the classical seesaw argument consumes next.  What it does not
248	supply is the evaluation map `π^*π_*L → L`; see the module docstring. -/
249	theorem rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one_of_pic0 (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π)
250	    [IsNoetherianRing B] (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom) (hg : genus C = 0)
251	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k B))
252	    (h : picEtAffineEquiv C B (lam : picEt C (overSpec k B))
253	      = PicEtAff.unit C B (relPicMk C (overSpec k B) D.cechPicClass))
254	    (p : PrimeSpectrum B) :
255	    Module.rankAtStalk (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0) p = 1 :=
256	  D.rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one_of_genus_zero hπ hg (D.htriv_of_pic0 hg lam h) p
257	
258	end BasicOpenCocycleDatum

260	/-! ## The presentation binder is FREE for classes from `relPic`
261	
262	The correction recorded in the module docstring, made usable.  `picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt`
263	(`Picard/PicEtUnit.lean:161`) holds at an arbitrary test **ring**, so for a `pic⁰` class whose
264	underlying `picEt` class comes from `relPicToPicEt` the presentation is not a hypothesis at
265	all — it is produced, and with it the datum. -/
266	
267	/-- **The presentation, produced at a test ring**, for a class in the range of `relPicToPicEt`.
268	
269	No field, no curve section, no `IsProper`-flavoured input beyond the standing binders: the
270	ring-level affine-consistency lemma gives the `unit` form directly, and
271	`exists_datum_pic0_presentation` upgrades it to the datum form. -/
272	theorem presentation_of_relPicToPicEt (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
273	    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite π]
274	    (z : relPic C (overSpec k B)) :
275	    ∃ D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π,
276	      picEtAffineEquiv C B (relPicToPicEt C (overSpec k B) z)
277	        = PicEtAff.unit C B (relPicMk C (overSpec k B) D.cechPicClass) :=
278	  exists_datum_pic0_presentation C B π _ ⟨z, picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt C B z⟩
279	
280	/-- **`π_*L` IS INVERTIBLE WITH NO PRESENTATION BINDER**, for a degree-zero class coming from a
281	relative Picard class over an arbitrary Noetherian test ring, at genus `0`.
282	
283	This is the form the earlier statements should have had: the only hypotheses left are the
284	membership itself, that the class comes from `relPic` (`hz`), the covering datum and the
285	engine's `IsNoetherianRing`.  The datum is existentially produced rather than supplied.
286	
287	**Non-vacuity of `hz`, stated at the level it is actually known.**  `hz` holds at the trivial
288	class (`map_one`, verified), so the statement is not empty.  Whether it holds at a *non-trivial*
289	degree-zero class is precisely the open surjectivity of `relPicToPicEt` discussed above — the
290	classes satisfying it form the intersection of `pic0Subgroup` with a subgroup, and this file
291	does not measure that intersection.  So: non-vacuous, and non-vacuous at a degenerate value
292	until that surjectivity lands. -/
293	theorem exists_rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one_of_relPicToPicEt (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
294	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
295	    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] [IsNoetherianRing B]
296	    (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite π] (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
297	    (hg : genus C = 0) (lam : pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k B))
298	    (z : relPic C (overSpec k B))
299	    (hz : (lam : picEt C (overSpec k B)) = relPicToPicEt C (overSpec k B) z) :
300	    ∃ D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π,
301	      ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum B, Module.rankAtStalk (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0) p = 1 := by
302	  obtain ⟨D, hD⟩ := presentation_of_relPicToPicEt C B π z
303	  exact ⟨D, fun p => D.rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one_of_pic0 hπ hg lam (by rw [hz]; exact hD) p⟩
304	
305	/-! ## Non-vacuity at `ℙ¹` -/
306	
307	/-- **The invertibility of `π_*L` at `ℙ¹` over an arbitrary field**, with the genus hypothesis
308	discharged by `Curve/P1H1Vanishing.lean`.
309	
310	Recorded because the chain above is worth nothing if its curve hypothesis has no witness; the
311	remaining hypotheses are the membership, its cocycle presentation, the covering map datum and
312	the engine's Noetherian binder — none of them about the genus. -/
313	theorem P1.rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one_of_pic0 (k : Type u) [Field k]
314	    {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] [IsNoetherianRing B]
315	    {π : (P1.asOver k).left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π]
316	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum (P1.asOver k) B π)
317	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = (P1.asOver k).hom)
318	    (lam : pic0Subgroup (P1.asOver k) (overSpec k B))
319	    (h : picEtAffineEquiv (P1.asOver k) B (lam : picEt (P1.asOver k) (overSpec k B))
320	      = PicEtAff.unit (P1.asOver k) B
321	          (relPicMk (P1.asOver k) (overSpec k B) D.cechPicClass))
322	    (p : PrimeSpectrum B) :
323	    Module.rankAtStalk (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0) p = 1 :=
324	  D.rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one_of_pic0 hπ (P1.genus_asOver_eq_zero k) lam h p
325
